model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral grammar for typed dependency relations between identified subjects, and for declaring how far downstream impact may legitimately be traced along each relation type.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-037 is a mixin that any subject model may attach to its entities. It defines what a dependency edge is, which referent classes may sit at each endpoint, which typed kinds exist and how the kind space is partitioned, the nature of the assertion (functional requirement, resource consumption, compatibility, ordering, or non-dependency co-location), the lifecycle phase in which the relation holds, the qualifiers that weaken, negate or condition it, the identity and validity interval of the assertion itself, how the assertion was determined and with what evidence and completeness, and whether the kind licenses downstream impact traversal. Bindings to external dependency vocabularies are recorded as alignments with explicit mapping strength and residue. The model is declarative throughout: it states that relations exist and what may be inferred from them; it does not resolve, install, build, test, deploy, observe, evaluate, enforce or compute closure over them.
in_scope: Typed dependency edges between identified endpoints, each carrying a canonical direction, permitted endpoint referent classes, permitted cardinality and lifecycle-phase scope.
A governed kind register partitioned so that no two registered kinds share semantics, with per-kind version or compatibility expression rules and documented false-positive exemplars.
Nature discrimination between functional requirement, resource consumption, compatibility constraint, ordering constraint and mere co-location or correlation.
Qualifier semantics: optional, peer, development, transitive, bundled or vendored, platform-provided, capability-satisfying, negative or conflicting, and circular relations.
Determination method (declared, discovered, inferred), evidence references, confidence limits and explicit completeness or known-unknown assertions per subject and kind scope.
Declarative per-kind impact-propagation licence: traversal direction relative to the edge, transitivity limits and stop conditions.
Crosswalk bindings to external dependency vocabularies and manifest grammars, recorded as alignment with mapping strength and unmapped residue.
Non-technical relations (organizational, contractual, operational) typed with the same edge grammar and qualified as influence when an adopting Dimension declares such kinds.
out_of_scope: Package resolution, installation, build, test or deployment execution, and any orchestration of those activities.
Vulnerability detection, severity scoring, reachability analysis and exploitability assertions.
Runtime traffic observation, call-graph extraction, tracing and telemetry collection.
Computation, storage or serving of transitive closure, blast-radius sets, criticality scores or ranked impact lists.
Component inventory mastering, licence determination and assembly or signing of bill-of-materials documents.
Secret values, credentials, private keys and any key material; only opaque references are carried.
Change approval, notification, enforcement, remediation and retention of the durable audit trail.
Data value lineage and record-level derivation history.

boundary_notes.distinction: Inventory masters the existence, identity, version and licence of components and services and assembles BOM documents; this model masters only the typed edge between two already-identified endpoints and the assertion about that edge. The CycloneDX dependency object references components by bom-ref rather than restating them, which is the same separation.

Reachability asks whether a defect in a target is exercised by a source; that is an analysis over edges plus code and runtime facts, and it is owned elsewhere. This model supplies typed edges and propagation licences as inputs and never asserts reachability, severity or exploitability.

PROV records past, instance-level influence of activities and entities (used, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom). A dependency edge is a forward-looking, type-level requirement that a target be present, compatible or ordered. Lineage may serve as evidence for a discovered edge but is not itself a dependency fact.

SLSA provenance attests which artifacts were actually fetched during a build and states that completeness is best effort. This model cites such attestations as evidence for build-time edges; generating, signing and verifying provenance and executing builds remain with that neighbour.

TOSCA requirements, capabilities, node filters and occurrences are processed by an orchestrator that instantiates and sequences nodes. This model reuses the requirement/capability shape to type hosting, connection, attachment and routing edges, but performs no matching, instantiation or ordering execution.

SPDX distinguishes a configures relationship from the configuration content itself. This model records that a subject is configured by, or trusts, a referenced item; issuance, rotation, storage, revocation and value custody stay with the managing model.

This model declares whether a kind licenses traversal and where traversal must stop. Selecting a starting subject, walking the graph, ranking affected items, notifying owners, enforcing gates and retaining the audit trail are owned by the change and incident model.

OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents own operation, channel, server and binding definitions and their own $ref resolution. This model carries the contract URI, the referenced operation or channel and the compatibility constraint; it does not restate or validate contract content.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - Core Model, RelationshipType vocabulary
sources.relevance: Normative relationship terms used as the anchor for typed dependency kinds: dependsOn, hasPrerequisite, hasRequirement, hasProvidedDependency, hasOptionalDependency, hasDependencyManifest, configures, hasInput, hasOutput, each defined as holding 'during a LifecycleScopeType period'.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - Core Model, LifecycleScopeType vocabulary
sources.relevance: Normative phase vocabulary (build, design, development, runtime, test, other) used to scope edges by lifecycle phase; the absence of a deploy value is the evidence for the recorded phase-alignment gap.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 2.3 - Relationships between SPDX elements
sources.relevance: Prior-generation scoped relationship types (DEPENDS_ON, DEPENDENCY_OF, BUILD_DEPENDENCY_OF, DEV_DEPENDENCY_OF, TEST_DEPENDENCY_OF, RUNTIME_DEPENDENCY_OF, OPTIONAL_DEPENDENCY_OF, PROVIDED_DEPENDENCY_OF, DEPENDENCY_MANIFEST_OF, STATIC_LINK, DYNAMIC_LINK, CONTAINS, PREREQUISITE_FOR) and their inverse-direction pairs; source of the direction-normalisation and mapping-residue rules.

sources.title: CycloneDX Bill of Materials JSON Schema, version 1.6
sources.relevance: Defines the dependency object (ref, dependsOn, provides) as 'the direct dependencies of a component, service, or the components provided/implemented by a given component', and states that objects absent from the dependency graph 'may have unknown dependencies' and must be treated as opaque rather than dependency-free; also the compositions completeness concept and externalReference type enumeration.

sources.title: ECMA-424 - CycloneDX Bill of materials specification
sources.relevance: Formal standardisation of the CycloneDX format covering components, services, dependencies, vulnerabilities and other supply-chain elements; used to cite CycloneDX as a versioned external vocabulary that must be pinned by edition when a crosswalk binding is recorded.

sources.title: TOSCA Version 2.0
sources.relevance: Requirement and capability model: 'Requirements express that a component depends on a feature provided by another component, or that the component has certain requirements against the hosting environment'; capabilities are 'features exposed by components that can be targeted by requirements'. Supplies source/target directionality, occurrences as cardinality, node filters, and the fact that v2.0 removed bundled Simple Profile relationship types.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Influence, usage and derivation semantics (wasInfluencedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, wasGeneratedBy, wasInformedBy) and the qualified-influence pattern (Influence, Usage, Derivation, qualifiedUsage) used to express observed and inferred edges with attached qualifiers, and to fix the boundary between past instance-level influence and forward-looking requirement.

sources.title: Debian Policy Manual - Chapter 7: Declaring relationships between packages
sources.relevance: Ecosystem-specific but rigorously defined relation grammar: Depends, Pre-Depends (ordering), Recommends, Suggests, Enhances (inverse of Suggests), Breaks, Conflicts (negative), Provides (virtual package / capability), Replaces, and Build-Depends / Build-Depends-Indep / Build-Conflicts; plus version relation operators (<<, <=, =, >=, >>) and alternatives. Primary evidence that negative, ordering and capability relations are first-class and are not expressible as dependsOn.

sources.title: package.json - npm CLI configuration reference
sources.relevance: Ecosystem-specific qualifier semantics: peerDependencies express 'the compatibility of your package with a host tool or library, while not necessarily doing a require of this host'; optionalDependencies allow the consumer to 'proceed if it cannot be found or fails to install'; bundleDependencies are included in the published tarball; plus devDependencies, overrides, engines, os and cpu platform constraints.

sources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
sources.relevance: Normative MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH meaning, the requirement that software using it MUST declare a public API, pre-release and build-metadata syntax, and precedence rules (build metadata ignored, pre-release lower precedence). Used for the register's own compatibility rules and, only where an ecosystem declares SemVer, for version-constraint interpretation.

sources.title: SLSA Provenance (predicate specification)
sources.version_or_date: v1.0 predicate (v1.2 is the current approved release)
sources.relevance: buildDefinition.resolvedDependencies is defined as the 'unordered collection of artifacts needed at build time' with the explicit caveat that 'completeness is best effort'; ResourceDescriptor (uri, digest, name, downloadLocation, mediaType, annotations) is the shape used for evidence references bound to build-time edges.

sources.title: OpenAPI Specification v3.1.0
sources.relevance: Reference Object ($ref) resolution against a base URI, operationId as a unique operation identifier and operationRef as a location reference, the Link Object as a design-time link between a response and an operation, and the statement that a document may be divided into multiple connected parts. Grounds interface-contract endpoints and the compatibility edge to a named operation.

sources.title: AsyncAPI Specification 3.0.0
sources.relevance: Servers as brokers, channels with addresses, operations declaring send or receive against a channel $ref, and protocol bindings. Grounds the separation of produce-side and consume-side stream edges and the distinction between a channel contract endpoint and a broker/server endpoint.

sources.title: ECMA-427 - Package-URL (PURL) Specification
sources.relevance: Standardised seven-component package identifier used across software supply chains and SBOMs, where the type component determines ecosystem-specific meaning of the remaining components. Basis for the governed global identifier tier for package-class endpoints, and for the warning that type semantics are defined outside the standard itself.

sources.title: Framing Software Component Transparency: Establishing a Common Software Bill of Materials (SBOM), Third Edition
sources.organization: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), United States
sources.version_or_date: Third edition, dated 3 September 2024, published 15 October 2024
sources.relevance: Public-authority guidance that an SBOM unable to convey the full transitive set must explicitly acknowledge 'known unknowns' so a consumer can distinguish a component with no further dependencies from one with unknown or partial dependencies, and that completeness does not propagate uniformly down the dependency hierarchy. Basis for the mandatory completeness assertion and the prohibition on reading absence as independence.

bundles.name: Typed dependency taxonomy
bundles.description: Everything needed to decide what an endpoint is, which single dependency kind applies, what the edge actually asserts, in which lifecycle phase it holds, and which qualifiers weaken, condition or negate it.
bundles.rationale: Every downstream use of a dependency fact - impact tracing, export to an SBOM, orchestration, review - depends first on the edge being typed unambiguously. Primary vocabularies disagree on granularity (SPDX 2.3 enumerates scoped dependency types, SPDX 3.0.1 collapses them into dependsOn plus a lifecycle scope, CycloneDX offers only dependsOn and provides, Debian and TOSCA add negative, ordering and capability relations). A local, partitioned kind register with explicit facets is therefore required before any alignment can be recorded.

findings.name: Endpoint referent classes
findings.description: The closed set of classes that may occupy either end of a typed dependency edge, and the rule that picks exactly one class when a candidate could be read as several. Classes span source artifacts and distributable packages or modules; source, build and test toolchain tools; deployed runtime services; interface contracts (API operations, message channels, wire protocols); data sets and data streams; schemas and ontologies; configuration items; secret and trust material referenced opaquely; compute, network and storage resources; named deployment environments; and external managed platforms outside the adopting Dimension's control. Class assignment is what makes the per-kind endpoint-type constraints enforceable, and it is deliberately independent of the storage projection: a class is a semantic role, not a document type.

findings.name: Dependency kind register and per-kind facets
findings.description: The partitioned register of typed dependency kinds together with the seven facets each kind must declare: canonical direction, permitted referent class at each endpoint, permitted cardinality, lifecycle phase or phases, version or compatibility expression rule, whether the kind licenses impact propagation, and documented false-positive exemplars. Kinds are organised by referent family - packages and modules; source, build and test toolchains; runtime services; interfaces and protocols; data sets and streams; schemas and ontologies; configuration and secret references; compute, network and storage; deployment environments; trust material; external platforms - and are required to be mutually disjoint in semantics. Representative kinds include requires-package, statically-links, dynamically-links, bundles-vendored-copy, provides-capability, built-with-tool, tested-with-tool, builds-from-source, invokes-service, conforms-to-interface, produces-to-stream, consumes-from-stream, reads-data-set, validates-against-schema, configured-by, requires-secret-reference, hosted-on, attaches-to-storage, routes-through-network, deployed-into-environment, trusts-anchor, depends-on-external-platform, conflicts-with, must-precede and co-located-with, the last being an explicit non-dependency record. No single package ecosystem's semantics are adopted globally; ecosystem-specific rules are labelled at the binding, not baked into the kind.

findings.name: Nature of the asserted relation
findings.description: The discriminator that separates five distinct things routinely conflated under the word dependency: a functional requirement (the source cannot correctly build, start or operate without the target), a resource consumption (the source consumes capacity, quota or throughput the target supplies), a compatibility constraint (the source imposes a permissible range or shape on the target without necessarily invoking it, as with a peer relation), an ordering constraint (the target must reach a state before the source may proceed, as with a pre-dependency, without any ongoing requirement), and mere co-location or correlation (shared host, shared owner, shared release train, correlated failure timing) which is explicitly not a dependency. Nature is orthogonal to kind: two edges of the same kind may differ in nature, and nature is the primary determinant of whether an impact traversal is even meaningful.

layers.name: Lifecycle phase and requirement qualifiers
layers.description: When the edge holds, and the conditions, alternatives, version constraints and negations that change what the edge means for a consumer.

findings.name: Lifecycle phase scoping of the edge
findings.description: The phase or phases in which a dependency actually holds: design, development, build, test, deploy and runtime. Phase is the axis that SPDX 3.0.1 made explicit by defining relationships as holding 'during a LifecycleScopeType period', replacing the SPDX 2.3 practice of encoding phase into the relationship type itself (BUILD_DEPENDENCY_OF, TEST_DEPENDENCY_OF, RUNTIME_DEPENDENCY_OF). A single pair of endpoints may carry several phase-scoped edges with different qualifiers and different propagation licences: a compiler is a build-phase requirement and absent at runtime; a broker is a runtime requirement and irrelevant at build. Deploy is treated as a locally defined phase because no primary external vocabulary provides a normative value for it, and this is recorded as an open gap rather than presented as aligned.

findings.name: Conditionality, alternatives and version or compatibility constraint
findings.description: The qualifiers that change how a consumer must read an edge, and the grammar in which acceptable targets are expressed. Conditionality covers optional (the source proceeds without the target), peer (a compatibility expectation on a host that the source does not itself pull in), development-only, transitive versus direct, bundled or vendored (the target ships inside the source's distributed artifact), platform-provided (the target is assumed present and is not distributed), capability-satisfying (the target supplies a named capability that several providers could supply, as with a virtual package or a TOSCA capability), negative or conflicting (the target must not be present, or not at certain versions), and circular. Constraint expression covers declared ranges on an unresolved requirement versus resolved pins on a specific artifact, alternatives, and platform or engine restrictions. Grammars differ irreconcilably across ecosystems, so each expression is stored with the grammar identifier that governs its interpretation and precedence.

The model therefore carries the verbatim expression, its grammar identifier and the reference back to the declaring document, and nothing more.

bundles.name: Edge assertion, evidence and impact licence
bundles.description: Everything needed to trust a dependency fact and to know how far it may legitimately be carried: the identity and validity of the assertion, how it was determined and with what evidence and completeness, the declarative licence for downstream traversal, and the bindings to external vocabularies and neighbouring analyses.
bundles.rationale: A typed edge is worthless to an agent without provenance and a completeness statement: CycloneDX warns that objects absent from the dependency graph must be treated as opaque rather than dependency-free, CISA requires known unknowns to be stated explicitly, and SLSA states that resolved build dependencies are complete only on a best-effort basis. Equally, impact tracing is the most common misuse of dependency data, so the permission to traverse must be declared per kind and separated from the act of traversing, which belongs to a consumer.

layers.name: Edge identity, determination and evidence
layers.description: How an individual dependency assertion is identified, timed, attributed, evidenced and qualified for confidence and completeness.

findings.name: Edge assertion identity and validity
findings.description: The dependency edge assertion is a first-class record with its own identifier, distinct from both endpoints and from any document that happens to carry it. It binds a source endpoint reference, a kind code, a target endpoint reference, a phase set, a qualifier set and the pinned kind-register version, and it carries asserter identity, event time, observation time, a validity interval and an integrity binding to the content it describes. Assertions are append-only: a correction supersedes rather than overwrites, and a withdrawal is a tombstone that preserves the identifier so a consumer can tell 'this edge was withdrawn' from 'this edge never existed'. Endpoint re-identification or re-versioning does not silently mutate an existing assertion; it produces a new one with an explicit predecessor link.

findings.name: Determination method, evidence and completeness
findings.description: How the edge came to be known and how much may be concluded from it. Three determination methods are kept strictly distinct: declared (stated in a manifest, topology declaration, interface document or other authored artefact), discovered (derived from an observation such as a lockfile resolution, a build attestation of resolved dependencies, an image inventory or a telemetry record produced elsewhere), and inferred (concluded by heuristic, similarity or model, never directly stated or observed). Each carries an evidence reference back to the producing system, a confidence statement with named limitations, and a falsification condition. Separately, completeness is asserted per subject and per kind and phase scope, because a set of edges says nothing about the edges that are missing: an empty outgoing set must never be published or read as independence, and completeness does not propagate uniformly to transitive targets.

findings.name: Declarative impact propagation licence
findings.description: For each kind, a declaration of whether a downstream consumer is permitted to traverse the edge when tracing impact, in which direction relative to the edge's canonical direction, with what transitivity limit, and under what stop conditions. The distinction is deliberate: dependency direction points from dependent to dependency, whereas impact usually flows the other way, so the licence names the traversal direction explicitly rather than leaving it implicit. Stop conditions include a bundled or vendored target (impact stops at the containing artifact), a platform-provided target (impact leaves the Dimension's boundary), an optional qualifier, a negative relation, a change of referent class, a deployment-environment boundary, and any relation whose nature is co-location or correlation. The model declares and withholds permission; it never performs traversal, never computes or stores closure, and never ranks or scores what is reached.

findings.name: External vocabulary alignment and neighbouring-analysis boundary
findings.description: Bindings from local kinds, phases and qualifiers to external dependency vocabularies - SPDX relationship types and lifecycle scopes, CycloneDX dependsOn and provides with its compositions completeness assertion, TOSCA requirements and capabilities with occurrences, PROV influence and usage, package manifests and lockfiles, OpenAPI and AsyncAPI references, and infrastructure declarations - recorded with an explicit mapping strength and the residue that survives the mapping. Alignment is never conformance: a conformance claim requires published evidence. The same finding fixes the boundary against neighbouring analyses that consume or project dependency facts without being interchangeable with them: software composition analysis, vulnerability reachability, runtime call extraction and data lineage each answer a different question and are recorded as consumers or evidence producers, never as sources of typed dependency facts on equal footing.

composition.target: Host subject models that adopt the WM-XCT-037 mixin
composition.purpose: Any subject model may attach the edge grammar, nature and qualifier vocabulary, phase scoping and propagation licence to its own entities. The host keeps ownership of its entity identity, state and lifecycle; this mixin contributes only the relation surface.

composition.target: Software component, service and package inventory model of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Endpoints are referenced by master-system identifier or governed global identifier. This model does not master component existence, versions, licences or inventory completeness, and does not assemble or sign bill-of-materials documents.

composition.target: SPDX Specification relationship and lifecycle-scope vocabularies (2.3 and 3.0.1)
composition.purpose: Bind local kinds and phase codes to SPDX relationship types and LifecycleScopeType values with recorded mapping strength, direction normalisation and residue. SPDX retains ownership of its vocabulary semantics, versioning and conformance criteria.

Bind to dependsOn and provides and to the compositions completeness concept, pinned by edition. Document assembly, signing, vulnerability sections and BOM lifecycle remain with that specification and its tooling.

composition.target: OASIS TOSCA Version 2.0 requirement and capability model
composition.purpose: Reuse the requirement/capability shape, source-target directionality and occurrences as cardinality for hosting, connection, attachment and routing kinds. Node-filter matching, instantiation, sequencing and orchestration execution remain with TOSCA processors.

composition.target: W3C PROV-O influence, usage and derivation vocabulary
composition.purpose: Express discovered and inferred relations as qualified influence where that is the honest reading. PROV retains ownership of activity, agent and derivation provenance semantics; lineage is evidence for an edge, never an edge itself.

composition.target: Interface contract catalogue holding OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents

composition.target: Build and release provenance attestation model

owner_package_requirements: Name a single accountable steward for the dependency kind register, the referent-class register and the propagation licence profile, with a named deputy and an escalation path for overlap adjudication.

Declare the referent-class to master-system bindings the Dimension uses, so that every endpoint class has a stated authoritative identifier source and a stated fallback order before any edge is recorded.
Publish the pinned register version and its effective interval alongside every exported edge set, and require consumers to pin that version rather than track a moving head.
Bind the Dimension's own regulatory and reporting profile (for example a national or sectoral software-transparency expectation) explicitly, because this model deliberately selects none.
Declare the records-retention policy that governs tombstones, superseded assertions and deprecated register entries, since this model defines the record shape but not the retention period.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Kind codes, referent classes, nature codes, qualifier flags, phase codes and propagation licences are minted in a Dimension-governed namespace IRI that is distinct from every external vocabulary. Never mint or redefine identifiers inside SPDX, CycloneDX, TOSCA, PROV, purl or ecosystem-manifest namespaces; external terms are referenced by their published IRI or enumeration token together with the vocabulary version, and are never copied into the local namespace. Locally defined values that have no external counterpart (for example the deploy phase) carry an explicit local-extension marker so a consumer cannot mistake them for standard terms.
registry_links: SPDX RelationshipType and LifecycleScopeType vocabularies as the primary alignment registries for relationship terms and phase scoping.
CycloneDX dependency and externalReference enumerations, pinned by ECMA-424 edition, as the alignment registry for graph export.
The Package-URL type registry standardised as ECMA-427 for package-class endpoint identifiers and their canonical form.
OASIS TOSCA 2.0 requirement, capability and occurrences constructs as the alignment registry for hosting, connection, attachment and routing kinds.
W3C PROV-O as the alignment registry for qualified influence, usage and derivation when recording discovered and inferred relations.

canonicalization_rules: The canonical edge form is the ordered tuple: source endpoint reference, kind code, target endpoint reference, phase set, nature code, qualifier flag set, pinned register version. Qualifier flags and phase codes are serialised in lexicographic order by code so that two logically identical edges canonicalise identically.

Endpoint references are canonicalised to the highest available identity tier before comparison; purl references are normalised to their canonical form, and a digest is never substituted for an identifier.
All time values canonicalise to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset; UTC is written as Z, and a value lacking an offset is rejected rather than assumed.

An externally stated inverse relation (for example an SPDX 2.3 DEPENDENCY_OF, or a Debian Enhances relative to Suggests) is canonicalised into the kind's declared direction, with the original term, its vocabulary and its version retained in the binding record.
Verbatim constraint expressions are never rewritten during canonicalisation; only the surrounding record is normalised, because rewriting an expression outside its own grammar changes its meaning.
patch_rules: Changing a kind's canonical direction, endpoint class constraints, cardinality bounds or propagation licence issues a new register or profile version; in-place editing of a published facet is prohibited.

Edge assertions are append-only. A correction is a superseding assertion that cites the superseded identifier, the reason and a new event time; a withdrawal is a tombstone that retains the edge identifier.

Retyping an existing edge to a different kind requires an explicit remap record naming the adjudicator, the old and new kind codes and the register versions involved; bulk silent retyping is prohibited.
Deprecating a kind requires a successor mapping or an explicit statement that no successor exists, and the deprecated entry stays resolvable for the Dimension's declared retention interval.
compatibility_rules: The register's published interface follows Semantic Versioning discipline: adding a kind, phase or qualifier is a minor change; removing or narrowing a kind, reversing a canonical direction, tightening endpoint constraints or revoking a propagation licence is a major change.
Consumers must pin the register and profile versions they were built against; consumption of an unpinned moving head is non-conforming and its results may not be published as governed edges.
A major register version obliges consumers to re-evaluate any stored classification decision; the model publishes the successor mapping but performs no automatic migration of consumer state.

Alignment bindings are versioned against the external vocabulary edition; when an external vocabulary issues a new edition, existing bindings remain valid for their pinned edition and a new binding row is created rather than the old one being edited.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the endpoint or the edge - for example the component registry's own key, the orchestrator's node or topology identifier, the interface catalogue's contract key, or the build system's run identifier. This is always preferred where it exists.

Governed global identifier or IRI where no master-system key is available: a Package-URL per ECMA-427, an SPDX element IRI, a CycloneDX bom-ref within its declared BOM scope, or an interface document URI plus its operation or channel reference.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension when neither of the above exists, recorded with an explicit Dimension-scoped marker so it is never mistaken for a globally resolvable identifier.

A version string, content digest, file path, hostname, timestamp or date is never an identifier. A digest may be carried only as an integrity binding attached to an identifier, and a date-derived value is rejected as a key at intake.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are RFC 3339 date-time values with seconds precision and an explicit numeric offset or Z; a local time without an offset is rejected rather than assumed to be UTC. Event time - when the dependency relation became true, changed or ceased to be true in the subject system - is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time - when the asserter detected the fact or when it was loaded into this model. Where the two differ, both are mandatory on every assertion; where they coincide, both are still recorded rather than one being inferred. Validity intervals carry their own start and end event times, and an open end means the relation is still asserted to hold, never that the end is unknown.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Governed entries are named by namespace plus code plus a monotonic version, and assertion series by identifier plus a monotonic sequence: register and profile entries as namespace/code@version (and namespace/kind-code/phase@version for licences), and edge assertions as edge-id#assertion-sequence. Sequence and version numbers are strictly increasing integers that never encode a date, a release name or an environment; all temporal meaning is carried by the effective interval, event time and observation time fields.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every published register version, licence profile version, crosswalk version and exported edge-assertion set carries a content digest computed over its canonical form together with the asserter or publisher identity. A consumer that cannot verify the digest must treat the set as unverified and must not publish derived governed edges from it. Digests bind content only and never serve as identifiers; an assertion whose recorded endpoint digest no longer matches the referenced content is flagged as stale rather than silently updated.

policies: One edge carries exactly one kind code, one nature code and one canonical direction. A relation that genuinely requires two kinds becomes two edges, each with its own qualifiers, evidence and propagation licence, so that a consumer never has to disambiguate a compound edge.

Co-location, co-residency, shared ownership, shared release train and temporal correlation are recorded as non-dependency observations carrying a non-propagating flag, and never license impact traversal regardless of how strong the correlation is.

Absence of an edge is never published or interpreted as evidence of independence. Every published edge set is accompanied by a completeness assertion for its kind and phase scope, with known unknowns stated explicitly, and completeness is never inherited by transitive targets.

Secret material, credentials, private keys and trust material are referenced by opaque identifier only. No secret value ever enters this model in any field, including free-text justification, evidence notes and residue notes.

External vocabulary terms are cited with vocabulary identifier and pinned version, with mapping strength and residue recorded. Conformance to an external specification is never claimed without published conformance evidence; alignment is the default and only claim.

Determination method constrains use: an inferred edge may never be exported as a declared edge, and a discovered edge must retain its evidence reference and the identity of the producing system when exported.

read: Resolve a kind entry, a referent class, or a propagation licence at an explicitly pinned register or profile version, with the effective interval returned alongside.

Retrieve edge assertions for a subject filtered by kind, nature, phase, determination method and validity interval; every such read returns the accompanying completeness assertion for the requested scope, and a read whose scope has no completeness assertion returns a warning rather than an apparently empty result.

Reads are as-recorded: supplying an as-of time returns the assertions that were current at that time, including superseded and withdrawn ones with their termination reasons, so history is never silently collapsed to the latest state.
Reads of an edge whose endpoints carry differing access classifications return the more restrictive treatment, which may include returning the kind and phase while withholding the target reference.
create: Register a referent class or dependency kind only with a cited source or a recorded Dimension-local justification, an overlap adjudication against every existing entry, and a named accountable steward.

Create an edge assertion only after both endpoints resolve to a registered referent class and carry an identifier from tier one or tier two, and only after a determination method and, for discovered or inferred methods, an evidence reference are supplied.
Every creation records asserter identity, event time and observation time; a creation missing either time axis is rejected rather than defaulted.
Creation of an edge matching a recorded false-positive exemplar for its kind is rejected with that exemplar cited in the rejection.
update: Kind, referent-class and licence facets are updated by issuing a new version with a successor mapping; the prior version remains resolvable and consumers pinned to it are unaffected.

Edge assertions are never edited in place. A superseding assertion cites the superseded identifier, the reason for supersession and its own event and observation times, and inherits the edge identifier while taking the next assertion sequence.
Retyping an edge to a different kind requires an explicit remap record naming the adjudicator, the old and new kind codes and both register versions; the superseded classification remains readable.
Updating a completeness assertion creates a new assertion with a new as-of time rather than amending the previous claim, so that the history of what was known when remains inspectable.
delete: This model performs no hard deletion of its own records by default. Withdrawal is a tombstone assertion that retains the edge identifier, kind code, endpoint class references, retraction reason, retraction event time and asserter identity, so a consumer can distinguish an edge that was withdrawn from an edge that never existed and from an edge that merely expired.

Retention periods, legal holds and physical disposition of this model's records are set and executed by the adopting Dimension's records-retention policy. This model defines the tombstone shape and the minimum fields that must survive disposition; it neither defines the retention period nor executes destruction, and it holds no enforcement authority over either.

Where content must be erased rather than tombstoned - for example a secret reference that leaked into an evidence field, or a personal identifier in an asserter field - the owning secrets-management or identity model executes the erasure under its own policy, and this model retains only the tombstone, a redaction marker naming the executing model, and the redaction event time.

Deprecated register, licence and crosswalk entries are retained with their successor mapping for at least the Dimension's declared retention interval before any disposition, because consumers pinned to an older version must still be able to resolve what they were built against.

Deletion propagation is explicitly not performed: withdrawing an edge never deletes, alters or cascades into either endpoint's record, and any downstream consequence is decided and executed by the referencing model that owns those records.

roles.name: Dependency kind steward
responsibilities: Maintain the kind and referent-class registers, run the disjointness test on every proposal and record the overlap adjudication.
Approve canonical direction, endpoint class constraints, cardinality bounds, permitted phases and false-positive exemplars for each kind.
Publish register versions with effective intervals and successor mappings, and decide deprecation.

roles.name: Edge asserter
responsibilities: Classify candidate relations against the pinned registers and record assertions with determination method, evidence references, event time and observation time.
Park ambiguous candidates as unclassified rather than defaulting them to a generic requirement kind.
Issue superseding and tombstone assertions for corrections and withdrawals, never editing prior records.

roles.name: Alignment custodian
responsibilities: Maintain crosswalk bindings to external vocabularies with pinned versions, mapping strength, direction normalisation and residue notes.
Record conflicts where two external vocabularies cannot both be honoured, rather than forcing a nearest-term mapping.
Withhold any conformance claim until published conformance evidence exists, and keep the default claim status at alignment only.

roles.name: Referent identity binder
responsibilities: Bind endpoints to master-system identifiers and governed global identifiers according to the identity priority, and mark Dimension-minted surrogates as such.
Escalate unresolvable endpoints rather than minting duplicate surrogates, and reconcile duplicates when a master-system key later becomes available.
Maintain the control-boundary classification that drives export restriction for internal locators.

roles.name: Impact licence approver
responsibilities: Approve, narrow or revoke per-kind and per-phase propagation licences, traversal directions, transitivity rules and stop conditions.
Set and apply the evidence threshold before a discovered or inferred kind receives any licence.
Confirm that licences remain declarative and hand traversal, ranking, notification and enforcement to the consuming model.

roles.name: Completeness attestor
responsibilities: Record completeness assertions per subject and per kind and phase scope, with explicit known-unknown statements and as-of times.
Block publication of any edge set that lacks a current completeness assertion for its scope.
Prevent completeness claims from being inherited by transitive targets when edge sets are exported.

access.default_rule: Register-level content - referent classes, kind entries with their facets, phase codes, qualifier vocabulary and propagation licences - is readable by every agent operating within the adopting Dimension, because classification is useless if the vocabulary is hidden. Individual edge assertions inherit the more restrictive of the two endpoints' access classifications as determined by the owning endpoint models; this model applies that inherited classification and does not originate one.
exceptions: Edges whose target is secret material, a trust anchor or a non-public external platform are restricted to the endpoint owners and the referent identity binder; the kind, nature and phase may be disclosed while the target reference itself is withheld.

Edges naming an internal network path, storage locator, host name or non-public deployment environment are withheld from any external export; only the kind code and a coarse referent class are permitted to leave the boundary.

Draft register, licence-profile and crosswalk versions before publication are restricted to the kind steward, impact licence approver and alignment custodian, since an unpublished direction or licence could be acted on prematurely.
Evidence references pointing into restricted producing systems are exposed as opaque handles, with resolution left to the producing system's own access control rather than being brokered here.
audit_requirements: Every register version publication, kind retype, licence grant or revocation, completeness assertion, supersession and tombstone records the actor, the event time and the observation time in this model's own change record, with both times in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset.

Access decisions, their enforcement and the durable audit trail are executed and retained by the adopting Dimension's access-control and audit systems. This model supplies the classification inputs and stores only a reference to the resulting audit record identifier; it neither evaluates access policy nor holds the audit trail.
Any export of an edge set records which completeness assertion accompanied it and which register version was pinned, so that a later dispute about what was known can be resolved against the record.

required_fields: Dependency kind register URL with the currently pinned version
read_order: AGENTS.md - establishes name, type, and the five resolution URLs before any other action.
Specification URL - model purpose, scope statement, in-scope and out-of-scope lists and boundary notes, so the agent learns what it must not do before it learns what it can.
Referent class register and dependency kind register at the pinned version, including per-kind facets and false-positive exemplars.
Propagation licence profile - read before any impact question is answered, so that the agent knows which traversals it may license and that it performs none itself.
Storage type URL - the projection and canonical-form rules for the chosen storage, whether document, graph, relational, message or repository based.
Interface URL - the read, create, update, supersede and withdraw operations, their preconditions and the access scopes that apply.
Processes URL - classification, alignment, completeness attestation, supersession and deprecation procedures, including escalation paths for ambiguous candidates.

coverage.claim: This structure covers the typed dependency surface an agent needs in order to decide what an endpoint is, assign exactly one dependency kind with declared direction, endpoint constraints, cardinality, phase, version-expression rule, propagation licence and false-positive exemplars, discriminate what the edge actually asserts, record qualifiers and constraint expressions in their own grammar, identify and time the assertion with separate event and observation times, state how it was determined and how complete the set is, declare how far impact may be traced, and bind to external vocabularies as alignments with recorded residue. It is grounded primarily in SPDX 2.3 and 3.0.1, CycloneDX and ECMA-424, OASIS TOSCA 2.0, W3C PROV-O, the Debian relationship grammar, ECMA-427 and CISA transparency guidance. No claim of universal or exhaustive coverage is made: the kind register is explicitly extensible, hardware, machine-learning and cryptographic-material kinds are not enumerated, and no primary source prescribes a confidence scale for inferred relations.

checklist.notes: Endpoint identity is tiered (master-system key, governed global identifier such as purl or SPDX IRI, Dimension-minted UUID or ULID) and the edge assertion carries its own identifier distinct from either endpoint, with digests barred from serving as identifiers and date-derived keys rejected at intake.

Two lifecycles are handled separately: the phase in which an edge holds (design, development, build, test, deploy, runtime), and the lifecycle of the register and assertion records themselves (proposed, active, deprecated with successor; asserted, superseded, withdrawn).

Canonical direction, endpoint class constraints and cardinality are declared per kind; the kind space is required to be disjoint; nature separates functional requirement, resource consumption, compatibility, ordering and non-dependency co-location; alternatives, negation and circularity are recorded explicitly.

Validity intervals with start and end event times, separate event and observation times on every assertion, RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset enforced, and termination reason codes distinguishing expiry, retraction, supersession and phase exit.

Asserter identity, source artefact reference, determination method (declared, discovered, inferred), tool and method version, reproducibility statement and resource-descriptor style evidence references, aligned to PROV qualified influence without re-modelling lineage.

Six named roles with disjoint responsibilities; a named accountable steward is required per register entry; endpoint records, evidence, traversal and enforcement are explicitly owned by referenced models rather than here.

Structural conformance checking against pinned kind facets (direction, endpoint classes, cardinality, phase, qualifier compatibility, constraint well-formedness), integrity digest verification with an unverified verdict, and completeness gating before publication. Explicitly not runtime policy evaluation.

Default readable register with edge assertions inheriting the more restrictive endpoint classification; exceptions for secret, trust, internal-locator and draft content; evidence exposed as opaque handles resolved by the producing system's own controls.

Tombstone-by-default with the minimum surviving field set defined here; retention period, legal hold, disposition execution and any content erasure are owned and executed by the adopting Dimension's retention policy and the relevant secrets or identity model, with only a redaction marker retained locally. Deletion never cascades to endpoint records.

Crosswalk artifact with pinned external vocabulary versions, mapping strength, direction normalisation, residue notes, round-trip reversibility results, conflicts register, and a default claim status of alignment-only until published conformance evidence exists.
Kind assignment with recorded exclusions, disjointness testing, false-positive exemplars, and an explicit unclassified parking state so that ambiguity is preserved rather than resolved by defaulting.
Resource-consumption edges carry quantity, unit and a declared-reservation versus observed-draw flag with the observation referenced, not collected here.
Secret and trust material appear only as opaque references; no value may enter any field including free text; internal locators are withheld from external export.

Deploy-time is a genuine and widely used phase, but SPDX LifecycleScopeType offers no corresponding value and CycloneDX carries no phase facet at all. Deploy is therefore defined locally with a local-extension marker and recorded as unmapped residue rather than presented as aligned.

No consulted primary source prescribes a confidence scale, threshold or falsification standard for inferred relations. The model requires that a scale be named and its provenance recorded, but cannot supply a normative one, so cross-Dimension comparability of inferred edges is not achievable today.

Typed technical and information-system relations do not carry personal data by design. The only realistic exposure is a personal identifier in an asserter field, which is handled by the redaction path in the deletion rules and governed by the adopting Dimension's identity model rather than here.

known_omissions: Hardware and firmware dependency kinds are not enumerated; alignment to hardware bills of materials is deferred and would require a separate referent family with its own endpoint identity scheme.

Machine-learning model, training-data and cryptographic-material relations are referenced through the generic data-set, schema and trust-anchor classes but are not typed as dedicated kinds, so ML-BOM and CBOM alignment remains unproven.

Licence and copyleft propagation along dependency edges is deliberately excluded: it is a licensing analysis over a graph, not a dependency fact, and modelling it here would import obligation semantics this model has no authority over.
Edge weighting, criticality scoring and any quantitative ranking of impact are absent by design; the model licenses traversal but supplies no basis for ordering what is reached.

No normative cross-ecosystem comparison of version constraint expressions is provided, because none exists in the consulted primary sources; expressions are stored verbatim with their grammar identifier and are not compared across grammars.

Ecosystem-specific kind registers beyond the representative set named here (for example per-language module systems, per-orchestrator topology dialects) are left to the adopting Dimension to extend under the disjointness rule.

Bidirectional or mutual requirements are modelled only as two directed edges plus a cycle marker; no primary source consulted defines admissibility criteria for a dependency cycle, so escalation is left to the Dimension.
conflicts: SPDX 2.3 encodes phase into the relationship type (BUILD_DEPENDENCY_OF, TEST_DEPENDENCY_OF, RUNTIME_DEPENDENCY_OF) while SPDX 3.0.1 uses a single dependsOn qualified by LifecycleScopeType. The two generations do not map one-to-one, and SPDX 2.3 additionally supplies inverse-direction pairs (DEPENDS_ON versus DEPENDENCY_OF) that must be normalised on intake.

CycloneDX dependsOn carries no lifecycle phase, nature or conditionality facet, so any projection from this model into a CycloneDX dependency graph drops phase, nature and qualifier information; the reverse projection cannot recover them and must not invent them.

CycloneDX provides is a capability or specification implementation statement, not a dependency; treating it as an inverse dependsOn reverses meaning. Debian Provides is a comparable but not identical virtual-package mechanism, and neither maps cleanly onto the SPDX relationship set.

Debian Recommends, Suggests and Enhances have no counterpart in SPDX or CycloneDX, and Enhances is the inverse direction of Suggests. Breaks and Conflicts are negative relations that no dependsOn-shaped vocabulary can express, so a negative relation exported to such a vocabulary is silently lost.

npm peerDependencies constrains the host rather than declaring a requirement the package will itself install; mapping it to SPDX dependsOn both reverses the practical direction and misstates the nature as functional requirement instead of compatibility constraint.

TOSCA 2.0 removed the bundled Simple Profile types, so HostedOn, ConnectsTo, AttachesTo and RoutesTo are profile-defined rather than normative in the standard itself. They are recorded as alignment candidates carrying a profile identifier, not as normative anchors.

W3C PROV used and wasDerivedFrom are past-tense, instance-level statements about activities and entities, whereas a declared dependency is a forward-looking, type-level requirement. Treating lineage as dependency manufactures edges that were never required to exist.

The CycloneDX schema instructs consumers to treat an object absent from the dependency graph as opaque rather than dependency-free, while common tooling practice reads an empty dependsOn as an assertion of no dependencies. CISA guidance resolves this in favour of explicit known unknowns, and this model follows the specification and the guidance against the practice.

SemVer precedence, Debian version relation operators and other ecosystem range grammars order pre-release and metadata differently and are not mutually comparable; no consulted primary source defines a cross-grammar comparison, so none is asserted.
regional_assumptions: CISA guidance is United States federal guidance. Other regimes, including European product-cybersecurity legislation, may impose different transparency, depth or reporting expectations; the adopting Dimension must bind its own regulatory profile because this model selects none.

Package-URL is internationally standardised through Ecma, but individual purl type definitions and their canonicalisation rules live outside the standard and are maintained by the ecosystems themselves, so type semantics can drift and can differ between registries and their regional mirrors.

Deployment environment and region naming is entirely provider-specific and is not standardised by any consulted source; environment endpoints therefore rely on Dimension-local or provider-local identifiers and are not portable across providers.

Debian and npm rules cited here are ecosystem-specific and are labelled as such throughout; they are used as evidence that negative, ordering, peer and capability relations exist as first-class concepts, never as globally applicable semantics.

Availability and completeness of build provenance attestations varies by build platform maturity, so the evidence quality attainable for build-time edges differs between environments even within one Dimension.
adversarial_checks: Tested whether a single universal depends-on kind would suffice. Rejected: SPDX phase scoping, CycloneDX provides, TOSCA hosting with occurrences, and Debian Conflicts, Pre-Depends and Recommends cannot be collapsed into one relation without losing direction, negation, ordering or capability semantics that each source defines normatively.

Tested whether npm peerDependencies can be exported as SPDX dependsOn. Rejected: the peer relation constrains the host and does not cause installation, so the mapping would reverse the practical direction and misclassify a compatibility constraint as a functional requirement. Recorded as a narrower-with-residue mapping instead.

Tested whether PROV used and wasDerivedFrom can populate dependency edges directly. Rejected: PROV records what did influence a specific entity in the past, not what a subject requires; using lineage as a source would fabricate requirements that were never declared and would inflate any impact traversal built on them.

Tested whether an empty outgoing edge set may be published as no dependencies. Rejected on two independent primary grounds: the CycloneDX schema directs consumers to treat absence as opaque, and CISA requires known unknowns to be stated explicitly and warns that completeness does not propagate down the hierarchy. A completeness assertion is therefore a publication precondition.

Tested whether co-location, shared host or correlated failure timing licenses impact propagation. Rejected: TOSCA hosting is a declared requirement with defined source and target roles, whereas co-residency is an observation with no requirement semantics. Such relations are retained with a non-propagating flag so the observation is not lost and cannot be traversed.

Tested whether TOSCA normative relationship types could be cited as canonical anchors for hosting and connection kinds. Rejected: TOSCA 2.0 removed the bundled Simple Profile types, so those names are profile-defined. They are recorded as alignment candidates with a profile identifier rather than presented as normative.

Compared every bundle, layer, finding, artifact and function against each composition rationale for target-owned semantics. Traversal and closure computation, blast-radius ranking, reachability and exploitability determination, build and deployment execution, secret issuance and rotation, telemetry collection, access-policy evaluation, enforcement and durable audit-trail retention were all moved to REFERENCE links, out-of-scope entries or boundary notes; what remains locally is declarative typing, assertion recording, structural validation, permission declaration and alignment.

Tested whether the propagation licence amounts to owning impact analysis. Rejected as a boundary breach and narrowed: the licence grants or withholds permission and names stop conditions, it produces no closure, no ranked set and no notification, and the consuming change and incident model is named as the owner of traversal and its results.
